target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.scope: global commercial aviation under revised IATA accident criteria including Other Fatalities
evidence.observation: IATA lists seven fatal accidents in 2024. The five fatal jet accidents are Jeju Air B737-800 (179 onboard), SWISS A220-300 (1 onboard), Swiftair B737-400 (1 onboard), Singapore Airlines B777-300ER (1 onboard), and Japan Airlines A350-900 with five Other Fatalities on the other aircraft. The two fatal turboprop accidents are Voepass ATR72 and Safarilink DHC-8. Thus the Boeing target members are exactly Jeju, Swiftair and Singapore Airlines.
evidence.use: annual-universe, target-membership and external/other-aircraft fatality reconciliation

evidence.publisher: Singapore Ministry of Transport / Transport Safety Investigation Bureau
evidence.observation: Official investigation material identifies Singapore Airlines Boeing 777-300ER 9V-SWM on a scheduled passenger flight and records one passenger death; the occurrence is treated as an accident by the investigating authority.

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Lithuania, Transport Accident and Incident Investigation Division
evidence.observation: Official Lithuanian investigation material identifies the Swiftair Boeing 737-476/737-400SF commercial cargo accident near Vilnius and the death of the aircraft pilot.

evidence.publisher: Republic of Korea Aviation and Railway Accident Investigation Board (ARAIB)
evidence.observation: ARAIB identifies the Jeju Air Boeing 737-800 HL8088 accident at Muan and records 179 fatalities and two serious injuries.

evidence.source_title: 2024 Statistical Summary of Commercial Jet Airplane Accidents
evidence.scope: worldwide commercial jet fleet under Boeing definitions
evidence.observation: Boeing independently lists the Singapore Airlines 777-300ER, Swiftair 737-400 and Jeju Air 737-800 fatal accidents in its 2024 commercial-jet table, consistent with the three Boeing target memberships.

scope_issue.reason: IATA excludes the Azerbaijan Airlines Embraer 190 event as a security/conflict-zone event. Because the aircraft is non-Boeing, that source-taxonomy dispute does not change the 2024 Boeing target membership; it is retained as a scope note rather than used to define the historical Boeing outcome.

completeness_assessment.reason: The IATA accident list exhaustively identifies all seven fatal accidents and five fatal jets under a definition that includes Other Fatalities. Exactly three fatal jets are Boeing and all three have competent-authority evidence plus independent Boeing reconciliation. The conflict-zone exclusion affecting a non-Boeing Embraer does not alter the Boeing target set.

gate_effect: 2024 annual cell PASS; overall G1 remains BLOCKED until every required annual cell passes
